claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you are looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'll need to ask you a few questions about yourself and Alex to determine your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 18, his eligibility depends on his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications) or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you. 

Could you tell me when Alex's 19th birthday is, or roughly when he started this A-level course? I ask because Child Benefit can continue for young people in qualifying education until they turn 19 (or until a specific cut-off point after they turn 19 if they started the course before that birthday).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, he just turned 18 recently, so his 19th birthday won't be for quite a while yet - nearly another year away.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you, that's helpful. Since Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels, he still qualifies as a child for Child Benefit purposes.

Now I have a couple of questions about your own circumstances:

Are you currently living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

One more question: Is Alex living with you, or if not, are you contributing to the cost of supporting him (for example, paying towards his food, accommodation, or other living expenses)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one final question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ **Alex qualifies** as a "qualifying young person" because he is 18 years old and in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels)
- ✅ **You live in the UK**
- ✅ **Alex lives with you**
- ✅ **No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him**

You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex as long as he remains in qualifying education or approved training, up until he turns 19 (or until a certain date after his 19th birthday if he's still on the same course).

If you're not already claiming and would like to apply, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
